name: France

findings.reversal_of: Huawei radio access network equipment at Bouygues Telecom and SFR
findings.summary: ANSSI granted Huawei radio equipment only short (mostly three-to-five-year) licences and signalled non-renewal, a de facto phase-out by 2028; Bouygues (~3,000 antennas) and SFR (8,000+) began replacing gear from 2021 and sued for compensation.
findings.analyst_inference: Reversal of operational (tier 5) Huawei 4G/5G RAN at the two exposed operators, coded geopolitical (security-agency licensing under a 2019 order). The Globe and Mail page gave no explicit date; finding dated by Total Telecom's 22 July 2020 piece (paywalled; only its summary was readable). Orange and Iliad mainly use Nokia/Ericsson per the Globe and Mail. Completion of removal not confirmed, so still_current null.

findings.controller: Campus IA joint venture (MGX, Bpifrance, Mistral AI, Nvidia)
findings.summary: MGX, Bpifrance, Mistral AI and Nvidia formed a joint venture to build a 1.4 GW AI campus outside Paris, with construction expected from H2 2026 and operations by 2028; EDG, Sipartech, RTE, Bouygues and Polytechnique are also partners.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: owner-operator is a JV mixing an Emirati fund (MGX, third), French state bank and firm (domestic) and Nvidia (us); stakes not found. Tier 2 because the JV is formed but construction start was not confirmed. A WAM headline (unopened) reports a second site; not coded. Investment undisclosed.

findings.summary: Fluidstack signed an MoU with the French government for a 1 GW AI supercomputer, about EUR 10bn in phase one with close to 500,000 AI chips, targeting go-live in 2026 and scaling beyond 1 GW by 2028.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third on the basis that Fluidstack is a UK company (DCD says only that it was founded at Oxford University; nationality not confirmed in an opened source). No site, construction or financing confirmed in this pass. EUR 10bn not converted to USD.

findings.financier: Bank consortium incl. Bpifrance, BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole CIB, HSBC, La Banque Postale, MUFG, Natixis
findings.summary: Mistral AI raised US$830m in debt from Bpifrance, BNP Paribas, Credit Agricole CIB, HSBC, La Banque Postale, MUFG and Natixis for a 44 MW site at Bruyeres-le-Chatel, owned and run by French operator Eclairion.
findings.analyst_inference: Owner-operator Eclairion is French, so domestic; tenant Mistral AI is also French. Tier 4 = financing closed. Date from the unopened sources' URLs (late March 2026); DCD page undated in fetch. Lenders include foreign banks (HSBC, MUFG); recorded as financier only.

findings.summary: The debt-financed Mistral compute site at Bruyeres-le-Chatel is to house 13,800 Nvidia GB300 Grace Blackwell GPUs, with operations planned to start by end of June.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 3 inferred from GPUs tied to a closed financing; no Nvidia order or delivery documentation found. Year of the end-June start not stated in fetched text (presumably 2026); whether operational not confirmed.

findings.summary: GENCI and CNRS chose Eviden to add 1,456 Nvidia H100 GPUs to the Jean Zay public supercomputer, funded by a EUR 40m France 2030 grant, with installation in April 2024 and user availability expected early summer 2024.
findings.analyst_inference: Accelerator vendor Nvidia (us) sets the pole; integrator Eviden (French) recorded as builder. Coded tier 4 (award plus installation scheduled); full operation not confirmed in this pass. EUR 40m grant includes EUR 10m for staffing per CNRS, so not entered as a hardware value.

findings.summary: The French state signed a contract with Mistral AI to improve its public-servant assistant (formerly Albert, now Assistant IA), run by DINUM; Albert had previously used open models Mistral supplied free. Value undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Mistral AI is French and controls its weights, so domestic. Specific model names not stated. Acteurs publics (Jan 2026) says Assistant IA was deployed in October 2025; scale of use not confirmed.

findings.summary: The Armed Forces ministry signed a framework agreement letting its entities, plus CEA, ONERA and SHOM, deploy Mistral AI models and tools on state-controlled infrastructure, steered by the defence AI agency AMIAD. Value and duration undisclosed.
findings.analyst_inference: Weights from a French provider, deployed on ministry infrastructure, so domestic. Framework agreement with a named counterparty coded tier 3; call-off orders not seen.

applications.null_reason: one search on Hikvision/algorithmic video-surveillance found only advocacy and parliamentary amendment documents; no named PRC-vendor safe-city deployment or removal order found

power.null_reason: no dedicated AI/data-centre power plant surfaced; only general reporting on France offering nuclear power to AI firms (snippet only)

Which vendors replaced Huawei at Bouygues and SFR, and confirmation of Orange/Iliad (Free) RAN and core vendors (Nokia/Ericsson).
Campus IA (Fouju area?): JV shareholdings, whether construction started in H2 2026, and the reported second site.
Fluidstack 1 GW project: site, financing, construction status; any reversal or pause.
Mistral Bruyeres-le-Chatel site: confirm operational start date and GB300 delivery.
Jean Zay: confirm H100 partition operational; any later GENCI/EuroHPC exascale (Alice Recoque) accelerator vendor choice.
Assistant IA (ex-Albert): contract value, models used, deployment scale; France Travail adoption of Mistral (snippet only).
Any Hikvision/Dahua presence or removal in French public-sector video surveillance, and vendors of 2024 Olympics algorithmic video-surveillance trials.
US-pole data-centre campuses in France since 2023 (e.g. Microsoft, Amazon, Digital Realty, Brookfield) were not searched.
